related_datasets.notes: CM4AI October 2025 Data Release (Beta), University of Virginia Dataverse, version 2.1. That release contained perturb-seq, SEC-MS and IF image data but no AP-MS data.

CM4AI June 2025 Data Release (Beta), University of Virginia Dataverse, version 2.1, published 2025-07-01. That revision added RGB immunofluorescent images, corrected RO-Crate metadata, and changed naming conventions.

CM4AI March 2025 Data Release (Beta), University of Virginia Dataverse, version 1.4, published 2025-03-03. That release included perturb-seq in undifferentiated KOLF2.1J iPSCs, SEC-MS in iPSCs and derivatives, and IF images stated there as covering 563 proteins of interest per condition.
Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - Data Release, University of Virginia Dataverse, V1, the May 2024 release cited in the CM4AI preprint.

Clark T et al., "Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence: AI-Ready Maps of Human Cell Architecture from Disease-Relevant Cell Lines", bioRxiv preprint describing the CM4AI project, its goals, methods, standards, datasets, software tools, status and future directions.
Nourreddine S et al., "A Perturbation Cell Atlas of Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells", bioRxiv 2024, PMCID PMC11580897, cited as a related publication for the perturb-seq component.

Schaffer LV, Hu M, Qian G et al., "Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics", Nature 642:222-231 (2025). Describes a U2OS multimodal cell map produced by integrating AP-MS and immunofluorescence data with the Cell Mapping Toolkit; acknowledges Bridge2AI Program funding OT2 OD032742. Its data are a separate dataset from this release.

versions_available: Prior CM4AI data releases remain individually published and citable in the University of Virginia Dataverse: May 2024 (doi:10.18130/V3/DXWOS5), March 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/B35XWX, V1, version 1.4), June 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R, V2, version 2.1), October 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, V2, version 2.1), and June 2026 (doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, V2, version 2.0).
